title: Runtime telemetry gating and upgrade experiment log
content:
Purpose:
This doc captures an experiment-driven approach to gating Private deployment runtime/control-plane upgrades using telemetry-derived thresholds. The goal is to minimize blast radius for VPC / on-prem upgrades, provide deterministic rollback triggers, and produce a reproducible log of test runs that we can iterate on. Draft notes and action items below — meant for the SRE + runtime + private-deploy teams to iterate.

Scope and non-goals:
- Scope: upgrades that touch serving runtime binaries, control-plane agents, and API compatibility layers for Private deployments (VPC and on-prem appliance). Includes Terraform orchestration and local operator components.
- Non-goal: model weights or user data migrations (handled by separate migration runs).

High-level hypothesis and experiment design:
- Hypothesis: We can detect early regressions for upgrade candidates by combining three orthogonal telemetry families: latency P95/P99 delta, error-class spike (5xx types + decoding failures), and KV-cache hit-rate degradation.
- Experiment phases:
  1) Baseline capture (48h) — collect pre-upgrade telemetry and save as baseline fingerprint.
  2) Canary lane rollout (2–6 hosts) — run candidate binary with feature-flagged KV cache behavior.
  3) Telemetry gating evaluation period (30–120m depending on traffic) — evaluate gates.
  4) Decision: promote / pause / rollback.

Telemetry signals and proposed gates (initial):
- Latency: P95 increase > +20% OR P99 increase > +35% sustained for two 5m windows => fail gate.
- Errors: absolute increase in 5xx error rate by >0.5 percentage points and relative increase > 50% => fail gate.
- Decoding/failure modes: any increase in token-decoding errors (metric: runtime.decode_errors) > 10 events per minute => fail gate.
- KV-cache hit rate: drop > 15% absolute OR > 25% relative => pause promotion and run extended validation.
- Resource signals: GPU churn (OOM events) or sustained GPU util > 95% for 3 consecutive windows => pause.
- Infra drift: Terraform plan drift detected compared to expected TF state => immediate human review (do not auto-promote).

Verification jobs (automated sanity checks):
- Smoke test suite: end-to-end request to API + response checksum for deterministic routes.
- Prompt-based quality checks: 50 synthetic prompts (from internal eval set) with token-level diff thresholds registered to Conductor/quality checks.
- Auth and routing: check client certificate handshake and KMS unwrap for on-prem before/after.
- Backcompat API contract: run the API contract shim test (linear INF-AC-7) that exercises legacy + new headers.

Rollback triggers (automated):
- Any gate failure triggers automatic traffic shift back to previous variant (canary -> baseline) and alerts SRE on-call.
- If rollback triggered, instantiate a forensics job to pull: runtime logs, kernel crash traces, serving-hotpath profiles and a snapshot of token cache stats for 30m prior to the gate fail.
- Post-rollback: freeze auto-promotions for the candidate for 24h until root-cause triage completed.

Experiment runbook (play-by-play):
1) Pre-flight (T-72h):
   - Create experiment in Conductor with links to PRs and TF plan (GH PR #678).
   - Notify customers in affected Dedicated/Private cohorts (if any) via CS channel.
   - Run infra drift check: terraform plan --detailed-exitcode for all accounts.
   - Capture baseline telemetry (48h rolling).
2) T-1h:
   - Tag candidate build and push signed artifact to artifact registry (GCR/airgap bundle).
   - Stage canary hosts and ensure health probes green.
3) Canary rollout (T+0):
   - Shift 2–6 hosts to candidate with 10% traffic weight. Start gating timers.
   - Run smoke test and prompt-based checks; fail early on smoke failure.
4) Evaluate (T+30m..T+120m):
   - Monitor gates dashboard. If any gate trips, trigger rollback sequence.
   - If passes, increment traffic to 50% for extended validation.
5) Promote (T+4h..T+24h):
   - If candidate stable, schedule phased promotion with TF updates and operator notices.

Notes on air-gapped/on-prem specific controls:
- Artifact signing: every candidate for on-prem must be signed and checksum verified locally before install.
- No automatic remote rollback for completely air-gapped appliances; we must still provide a signed fallback artifact and an operator runbook for manual rollback.
- KMS: test decrypt roundtrip for customer KMS paths during canary — log success/failure counts.

Terraform and config drift considerations:
- Add tfworkspaces: a separate workspace per cluster for upgrade rehearsals.
- Before promotion, run terraform plan and capture plan-id in the experiment log. If plan changes produce resource replacements (create/destroy), require human approval.
- Record provider plugin versions and module checksum in the experiment metadata.

Run log template (to be appended to this doc for each experiment run):
- run_id: string (e.g., telemetry-gate-2025-01-22-01)
- candidate_tag: gh runtime tag or airgap bundle id
- baseline_window: ISO timestamps
- canary_hosts: list of host ids
- traffic_weight: numeric
- gate_outcome: pass|fail|paused
- notes: freeform text with links to PRs, logs, trace ids
(We will keep a simple CSV export of these run logs in S3 for analysis.)

Open questions / follow-ups:
- Threshold tuning: need more historical analysis to set initial gates; ticket created INF-2319 to run retrospective on last 6 upgrades.
- Chaos scenarios: do we want to inject controlled KV-cache evictions during canary to validate degradation signal? (Pros/cons discussed with Jules).
- Customer-facing communications: should we auto-signal customers when canary enters rollback? (CS feedback requested).

Action items (short):
- [ ] Diego: build dashboard with the gating rules and two alert severities (warning / fail) — due 2025-01-20.
- [ ] Priya: add tfworkspace rehearsal script and record module checksums — due 2025-01-18.
- [ ] Samir: wire the smoke tests into the canary pipeline and make failures block rollouts — due 2025-01-25.
